criteria.text: Given a Basecamp comment with '##Critique##', When the system processes the comment, Then a review item is created with status 'Pending'.
Given a comment with '## Review ##', When the system processes the comment, Then no review item is created.
Trust: The system logs the detection event with the exact comment ID.

stories.notes: All 3 criteria verified by tests (review_queue/test_intake.py, test_intake_routes.py, test_logging_config.py) and a live uvicorn+curl run. Comments come via a CommentSource interface with fixtures/HTTP; the live SQL Server reader for Basecamp_MessageBoards_MessageComments is deferred (needs credentials + driver). Review Queue is in-memory until a database is chosen. 2026-09-25 (user decision): '##Please Critique##' also creates the review item, with a marker_note reminding the student to write ##Critique## next time, audited as NONSTANDARD_MARKER; #Critique# and prose still do not count. Tests: backend/app/basecamp/test_critique_marker_detector.py, backend/app/review_queue/test_intake.py, backend/app/test_intake_routes.py. | 2026-09-28 (STORY-004 follow-up, user-approved): a comment that carries ##Critique## together with ##FeedbackGiven## or ##Approved## is a reviewer's comment and no longer creates a review item; audited as comment_no_marker with reason REVIEWER_FEEDBACK (13 of 553 in the history extract). Test: backend/app/review_queue/test_intake.py::test_a_reviewer_comment_quoting_the_critique_marker_creates_no_item.

criteria.text: Given a Basecamp project with submissions, when the system retrieves data, then it includes comments, attachments, and links.
Given a Basecamp project with no submissions, when the system attempts to retrieve data, then it returns an empty dataset.
Trust: The system logs all data retrieval actions with timestamps and user IDs.

stories.notes: All 3 criteria verified by tests against simulated Basecamp API responses (test_submission_retrieval.py: AC1 comments/attachments/links, AC2 empty dataset, trust audit log with timestamp + requested_by_user_id on success, failure and unexpected errors) and by retrieve_submissions.py --demo. NOT yet run against live Basecamp: no OAuth app is registered, and Basecamp offers no API keys. Failure paths tested: 429 (Retry-After, capped), invalid token (401/403, no retry), network failure/5xx (3 attempts). Retrieved comments feed STORY-001 intake unchanged (test_submission_comment_source.py); SQL and API comment ids are the same Basecamp recording ids.

criteria.text: Given a submission for ST0, When the system loads rules, Then only ST0 rules are loaded.
criteria.evidence: backend/app/rules/loader.py load_rules() loads only the identified Stress Test's module at the registry version (backend/app/rules/modules/registry.json -> ST0/v1.json, built word for word from docs/stress-test-rules/ST0-rules-v1.md); RuleModule (backend/app/rules/module.py) rejects any module carrying another Stress Test's rules; tests: backend/app/rules/test_loader.py::test_an_st0_submission_loads_only_st0_rules, backend/app/rules/test_module.py

criteria.text: Given a submission for an unknown Stress Test, When the system loads rules, Then it routes to manual resolution.
criteria.evidence: load_rules() returns outcome manual_resolution with a reason code (NO_RULE_MODULE, STRESS_TEST_NOT_IDENTIFIED, STRESS_TEST_AMBIGUOUS, plus not-found / invalid / version-mismatch / timeout / read-failed) and never guesses; tests: backend/app/rules/test_loader.py

criteria.text: Trust: The system logs rule loading events with rule version.
criteria.evidence: every load_rules() call writes one audit event (rules_loaded with stress_test_id and rule_version, or rules_manual_resolution with the reason code) and a JSON log line; if the audit write fails no rules are returned; tests: backend/app/rules/test_loader.py (Acceptance 3 section)

stories.notes: All 3 criteria pass. ST0 v1 is built only from the official ST0 Rules & Validation Specification (transcribed to docs/stress-test-rules/ST0-rules-v1.md) plus three dated user decisions: ST0-002 valid = link opens without an error; ST0-003 severity Required Fix; a submission split across comments is a reviewer note, not a failure. Rule loading is not yet called by any review flow (STORY-004 will call load_rules); the manual-resolution queue itself is STORY-008. ST1-ST5 have no module until their specs are provided (NO_RULE_MODULE).

criteria.text: Given a valid submission, When Claude evaluates it, Then structured draft findings are returned.
criteria.evidence: backend/app/evaluation/evaluate.py evaluate_submission(): input check + deterministic pre-checks, then Claude (claude-sonnet-5 via the official anthropic SDK, backend/app/evaluation/claude_client.py) per blocking stage with structured output (output_config.format from ClaudeStageAnswer); returns an EvaluationResult (backend/app/models.py) with passed rule ids and FAIL/ADVISORY DraftFindings carrying rule_id, status, severity (from the rule module), evidence, reason, suggested_feedback and confidence; answers that do not cover exactly the stage's rules are rejected; tests: backend/app/evaluation/test_evaluate.py::test_a_valid_submission_returns_structured_draft_findings, test_claude_client.py; demo: backend/scripts/evaluate_demo.py; live: 15 historical ST0 submissions evaluated with the real API (backend/scripts/compare_st0_history.py), 15/15 schema-valid

criteria.text: Given an invalid submission, When Claude evaluates it, Then an error is returned.
criteria.evidence: an incomplete or invalid submission raises SubmissionIncompleteError (SUBMISSION_EMPTY incl. screenshot-only, COMMENT_NOT_FOUND, SUBMISSION_TOO_LARGE, NOT_A_SUBMISSION for a reviewer's comment, RULES_NOT_LOADED) before any Claude call and nothing is stored; Claude failures raise typed errors (unreachable, timeout, auth, malformed, refused) after at most 2 retries; oversized input -> manual resolution; tests: backend/app/evaluation/test_input_check.py, test_evaluate.py::test_an_invalid_submission_returns_an_error_without_calling_claude, test_claude_failures_are_errors_and_can_be_retried_later

criteria.text: Trust: The system logs evaluation events with submission ID and rule ID.
criteria.evidence: every evaluation writes audit events carrying comment_id (submission id), message_id, stress_test_id and rule_version: evaluation_started, one evaluation_finding per evaluated rule with rule_id and PASS/FAIL/ADVISORY, evaluation_completed; failures write evaluation_failed / evaluation_manual_resolution with a reason code; replays write evaluation_already_done; plus JSON log lines; tests: backend/app/evaluation/test_evaluate.py::test_every_evaluated_rule_is_audited_with_submission_and_rule_id; demo output in backend/scripts/evaluate_demo.py

stories.notes: All 3 criteria pass (pytest 559/559, credential scan clean). Built with the user's token-saving rules: cached rule-module system prompt, plain text with [SELECTED] for the yellow highlight, deterministic pre-checks, structured output, pass list + FAIL/ADVISORY findings, Stage 2 only after a clean Stage 1, effort low, idempotent on (comment_id, rule_version), count_tokens + manual resolution above 20k tokens, per-call usage ledger with a daily token limit, 60 s timeout and at most 2 retries (Retry-After capped at 30 s). Live check on 15 historical ST0 submissions: $0.26 in total, cache hit on every call after the first; agreement hints in the git-ignored report. Found in the comparison: 13 of 553 critique detections in the history are reviewer comments quoting ##Critique## with ##FeedbackGiven##/##Approved##; the evaluator refuses them (NOT_A_SUBMISSION) and the STORY-001 intake now skips them (user-approved). Not yet: reviewer notes (CONTENT_NOT_IN_TEXT, SPLIT_SUBMISSION) are not produced; the thread reader (thread.py) is built but the evaluator does not yet use previous versions/feedback; the history store for final human feedback comes with the reviewer UI (STORY-005). Results/usage are local git-ignored JSONL files (SQL Server stays read-only).

criteria.text: Given a submission is processed, when an action is taken, then it is logged in the audit trail.
criteria.evidence: backend/app/audit/trail.py (append-only JSONL audit trail, fsync per event, AuditWriteError on failure) wired into backend/app/review_queue/intake.py (review_created / review_already_queued / comment_no_marker / comment_rejected_malformed) backend/app/routers/reviews.py (finalize_allowed / finalize_blocked) and backend/app/basecamp/submission_retrieval.py (retrieval_started / _completed / _failed); tests: backend/app/audit/test_trail.py, backend/app/review_queue/test_intake.py, backend/app/test_intake_routes.py, backend/app/test_finalize_audit.py, backend/app/basecamp/test_submission_retrieval.py

criteria.text: Given a submission is processed without human review, when the system attempts to auto-approve, then it blocks the action.
criteria.evidence: backend/app/guardrails/review_finalization_guardrail.py (assert_safe_to_finalize) enforced at POST /reviews/finalize-check (backend/app/routers/reviews.py); every blocked attempt returns 409 and is recorded as finalize_blocked with its reason code; tests: backend/app/guardrails/test_review_finalization_guardrail.py, backend/app/test_finalize_audit.py

criteria.text: Trust: The system ensures no credentials are stored in source code or shared documents.
criteria.evidence: backend/app/guardrails/credential_leak_guardrail.py + backend/scripts/scan_for_credentials.py (exit 0 across the repo); audit events have no free-text field and data/audit/ is git-ignored; tests: backend/app/guardrails/test_credential_leak_guardrail.py, backend/scripts/test_scan_for_credentials.py, backend/app/audit/test_trail.py, backend/app/review_queue/test_intake.py

stories.notes: All 3 criteria pass. Audit trail is an append-only JSON Lines file (data/audit/audit_trail.jsonl, git-ignored) rather than a SQL Server table: existing SQL Server tables and procedures must not change (user rule, 2026-09-25). Every intake outcome, every finalize-check attempt (allowed or blocked) and every Basecamp retrieval (started, completed or failed) writes an event; if the write fails the action is refused (503 over HTTP). Limitation: if the audit write fails right after a review item is created, the item stays and a re-run records it as review_already_queued (no transaction spans queue and audit without a database). Earlier Node-era evidence replaced with the Python files.

criteria.text: Given historical critique and feedback comments for a Stress Test are indexed in a vector database stored outside SQL Server, when a new submission for that Stress Test is reviewed, then the system returns the top 5–10 most similar cases from that same Stress Test only.
criteria.evidence: Cases (student ##Critique## submission + the reviewer's ##FeedbackGiven##/##Approved## answer, backend/app/history/cases.py) are embedded locally (fastembed bge-small-en-v1.5, backend/app/history/embedder.py) into LanceDB under the git-ignored data/vector_index/ (backend/app/history/lancedb_index.py), not SQL Server; retrieve_similar_cases() (backend/app/history/retrieval.py) filters to the Stress Test then returns the top HISTORY_TOP_K (default 10, allowed 1-15) by cosine similarity; the evaluator passes them to Claude (backend/app/evaluation/evaluate.py). Tests: backend/app/history/test_retrieval.py::test_found_returns_the_top_k_most_similar, test_lancedb_index.py::test_top_k_only / ::test_most_similar_first_same_stress_test_only. Live: real index 472 cases; backend/scripts/history_demo.py returned 10 ST0 cases (similarity 0.850-0.779) for an ST0 submission.

criteria.text: Given a submission for one Stress Test, when historical cases are retrieved, then no case from a different Stress Test is returned.
criteria.evidence: The Stress Test filter runs before ranking (LanceDB prefilter on stress_test_id, backend/app/history/lancedb_index.py), HistoryRetrieval (backend/app/models.py) rejects a case from another Stress Test, and retrieval reports an index that leaks one as ContractViolation rather than filtering it. Tests: test_retrieval.py::test_only_the_same_stress_test_is_returned (ST0/ST1/ST2 with exact-match decoys), ::test_an_index_that_leaks_another_stress_test_is_reported_not_used, test_vector_index.py::test_search_never_returns_another_stress_test_even_when_it_is_closer, test_evaluate_history.py::test_with_real_retrieval_only_the_same_stress_test_reaches_the_prompt. Live demo: the same text as ST3 returned ST3 only.

criteria.text: Given the vector database or the embedding service is unavailable, when retrieval runs, then the review continues without historical examples and the error is shown to the reviewer.
criteria.evidence: Every index and model call is bounded (backend/app/history/bounded.py: timeout per attempt, at most 3 attempts); an outage becomes HistoryRetrieval status 'unavailable' with error_class and a reviewer message 'Historical examples are unavailable (...); this review continues without them.', stored on EvaluationResult.history and audited as history_retrieved/failure; the evaluation runs both stages without examples; an unexpected lookup error is handled the same way (HistoryLookupFailed). Tests: test_retrieval.py::test_unavailable_returns_empty_with_a_visible_error, test_evaluate_history.py::test_an_unavailable_history_does_not_stop_the_review, ::test_with_real_retrieval_an_embedding_outage_still_evaluates, ::test_an_unexpected_error_in_the_lookup_does_not_stop_the_review, test_embedder.py, test_bounded.py. Live demo: missing index -> unavailable, evaluation stages [1, 2]. No reviewer UI exists yet (STORY-012): the message is on the result.

criteria.text: Given no similar historical cases exist, when retrieval runs, then the system returns an empty list and says so, rather than failing.
criteria.evidence: status 'none_found', cases [] and message 'No similar past reviews: no past reviews are indexed for ST5. The evaluation uses the ST5 rules only.' (backend/app/history/retrieval.py). Tests: test_retrieval.py::test_nothing_indexed_for_the_stress_test_is_an_empty_list_that_says_so, ::test_blank_submission_text_is_none_found_without_calling_the_model, test_lancedb_index.py::test_a_stress_test_with_no_cases_returns_an_empty_list, test_evaluate_history.py::test_none_found_is_on_the_result_and_the_prompt_has_no_examples. Live demo: an index with no ST0 cases -> none_found.

criteria.text: Trust: Historical examples never override the current Stress Test rules, and existing SQL Server tables and procedures are never changed.
criteria.evidence: Examples sit only in the user message, labelled 'They are NOT rules: the ST0 rules in the system prompt decide every verdict' (backend/app/evaluation/prompt.py); the system prompt (the rule module) is byte-identical with or without them; only the stage's rule ids are accepted and severity always comes from the module. Tests: test_evaluate_history.py::test_a_past_review_cannot_change_the_rules_or_their_severity, ::test_a_past_review_cannot_add_a_rule, ::test_found_cases_reach_both_stages_as_labelled_examples_before_the_submission, ::test_without_history_the_prompt_is_exactly_as_before. SQL Server: no .sql file or db module changed in this story; the index is LanceDB files; SQL Server was only read (the extract predates this story).

stories.notes: User decisions 2026-09-28: HISTORY_TOP_K setting, default 10 (meets 'top 5-10'; replaces the 2026-09-25 'top 15'); LanceDB embedded (matches the file-based stores of STORY-001/004/011); local fastembed embeddings (free, text stays local); STORY-004 prompt.py/evaluate.py changed additively (no history = identical prompts). No rule-id filter (historical feedback is not tagged by rule). First index: 472 cases from the 2026-09-25 per-Stress-Test extract. Completed reviews are not indexed yet (STORY-007). The reviewer sees the history message on the evaluation result; no UI yet (STORY-012).

criteria.text: Given a Basecamp user on the reviewer list, when they sign in with Basecamp, then they reach the Review Queue as a Reviewer
Given a Basecamp user on the admin list, when they sign in, then they can also add, remove and change the role of reviewers and admins
Given a Basecamp user on neither list, when they sign in, then access is refused with a clear message
Given no signed-in session, when any review page or API is opened, then the user is sent to sign in and nothing is shown or changed
Given a Reviewer, when they try an admin-only action, then it is refused
Given a signed-in user, when they sign out or 8 hours pass, then they must sign in again
Trust: every sign-in, refusal, sign-out and role change is logged with who and when, and no password or token appears in logs or the repo
